program_title: Erasmus Mundus European Master for Industry in Microwave Electronics and Photonics (EMIMEP) — successor to EMIMEO
degree_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's Degree (Master Universitario)
duration: 2 academic years (120 ECTS), based on consortium page references to 'first academic year' and 'second academic year'

admission_requirements.grade_requirement: Not found. No numeric GPA/grade threshold was published on any page reached (UPV/EHU accreditation page, EHU Erasmus Mundus apply page, or consortium emimeo.eu site).
admission_requirements.prior_degree: Program targets graduates in Electronics, Electrical Engineering, Telecommunications, Photonics, or Applied Physics (per third-party scholarship aggregator guides; not independently confirmed on an official page during this session).
admission_requirements.credential_recognition_note: Not found. No non-EU credential legalization/recognition requirement was stated on any page reached.
admission_requirements.other: Consortium: University of Limoges (coordinator), University of Brescia, UPV/EHU, Friedrich Schiller University Jena. Year 1: Limoges (semester) and Brescia (semester); Year 2: specialization at a chosen partner university including UPV/EHU (Bilbao). Students also attend a 'Research and Industrial Week' in Cluj (Year 1) and the 'European Microwave Week' at the start of Year 2.

language_requirements.english_certificate_required: Not explicitly confirmed on an official program page; third-party scholarship-aggregator guides (not official) list 'proof of English' among required documents alongside transcripts, CV, motivation letter, and references.

tuition.eu_eea_per_year_eur: Not found on official pages. Third-party aggregators describe Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders receiving EUR 1,400/month for up to 24 months with enrolment fees covered, plus tuition waiver, travel/visa support, and health/travel insurance — but this is EM scholarship funding, not a stated base tuition figure, and is not independently verified against an official EMIMEP page this session.
tuition.notes: Self-funded (non-scholarship) applications are described as 'now open' on the consortium site, implying a self-pay track exists, but no fee amount was found. Erasmus Mundus scholarship competition is the primary funding route typically advertised for this consortium.

deadlines.main_intake: 2026 cycle: EHU's own apply page states 'student applications are now open until Friday 13 March 2026.' A third-party guide cites a slightly different date (12 March 2026) for the general EMIMEP cycle — sources disagree by one day. Next full cycle (2027 intake) is reported by a third-party guide to open November 2026 with a March 2027 deadline, not yet officially published.
deadlines.notes: Erasmus Mundus scholarship application round for an earlier cycle was noted on the consortium site as opening '18 November 2024' with no closing date shown — this reference is for a prior admissions cycle and should not be relied on for 2026/27.

curriculum_notes: Direct access to a detailed syllabus/course-list page was not achieved this session (accreditation page had only verification/RUCT documents; consortium site gave only partner/location structure, not module list). Known structural detail: Year 1 split between Limoges and Brescia; Year 2 specialization at a chosen partner (UPV/EHU Bilbao is one option), with 'Research and Industrial Week' (Cluj) and 'European Microwave Week' as cross-cohort events.
vlsi_rtl_relevance_notes: Program core is microwave electronics and photonics (RF circuit design, microwave devices, photonic components, and their implementation in wired/wireless communications) per the consortium page's general description. This is strongly adjacent to RF/analog IC and photonic-IC design work, but a module-by-module curriculum (e.g., explicit RFIC, antenna, or photonic-integration course titles) could not be retrieved this session — syllabus pages behind EHU's site navigation ('Syllabus' link noted on the accreditation page) were not reachable/fetched.

degree_type: MSc (private, unaccredited as Spanish official title)
duration: Not explicitly stated as a total length; curriculum delivered in 3-week immersive modules rather than semesters. Degree is also offered at MEng level per the main harbour.space site.

admission_requirements.grade_requirement: Not found — no GPA/grade threshold stated on official pages reached.
admission_requirements.prior_degree: Not explicitly stated for the Master's tier; the general admissions FAQ says technical programs (CS, Data Science, Front-end Development, Cyber Security) require 'a solid foundational knowledge of mathematics, statistics, and programming' and admission follows a 'holistic review' of preparedness and career potential, plus a Maths and Computer Science entrance test (per third-party Mastersportal listing, not confirmed on an official page this session) and a CV/diploma submission.
admission_requirements.entrance_exam: A 'Maths and Computer Science Test' is referenced by a third-party aggregator (Mastersportal) as part of the process; not confirmed directly on an official Harbour.Space page this session.
admission_requirements.other: Official process description (from join.harbour.space): submit application, attend an interview, receive a decision 'within a week.'

language_requirements.english_certificate_required: Not found on official pages — no IELTS/TOEFL score was listed. A third-party Mastersportal summary explicitly states 'We are not aware of any English requirements for this programme,' which is a third-party inference, not an official confirmation of 'no requirement.'

tuition.eu_eea_per_year_eur: Spanish citizens: €11,450 (50% off standard €22,900) if applying before 31 May 2026 for Sept 2026 start — discount tier, not a distinct EU-wide rate.
tuition.non_eu_per_year_eur: International students: €17,125 (25% off standard €22,900) under the same early-application discount; standard/full tuition is €22,900 — currency not explicitly marked on the page but consistent with EUR elsewhere on the site.
tuition.notes: Figures are per the Computer Science programme page; 'per year' framing is inferred since Harbour.Space does not structure in standard academic years — treat €22,900 as the base full-program/tier price referenced, not confirmed as strictly 'per year.' Early-bird discount deadline: 31 May 2026 for a September 2026 start.

deadlines.main_intake: Recommended start dates: 7 September 2026 (Barcelona) or 17 August 2026 (Bangkok campus). Rolling admission — 'you can start every three weeks throughout the year.'
deadlines.notes: Discounted tuition requires applying before 31 May 2026.

curriculum_notes: Core modules listed on the official programme page: Software Engineering (Java/Spring), Mobile Development, Modern Web Application, Modern Software Architectures, Distributed Systems & Clouds, Computer Networking. Teaching emphasis described as 80% practice / 20% theory, delivered in 3-week immersive modules.
vlsi_rtl_relevance_notes: No VLSI/RTL/embedded/microelectronics content found — curriculum is software/web/distributed-systems focused, not hardware design. Low relevance to a VLSI/RTL background beyond general CS/software skills.

program_title: University Master's Degree in Computational Engineering and Mathematics (Màster Universitari en Enginyeria Computacional i Matemàtica)
duration: 60 ECTS / 1 academic year full-time (per third-party aggregator breakdown: 18 ECTS compulsory + 24 ECTS electives + 18 ECTS final master's project = 60 ECTS); delivered fully online.

admission_requirements.grade_requirement: Not found — no numeric GPA/grade threshold located.
admission_requirements.prior_degree: Open to graduates in computer engineering, mathematics, telecommunications engineering, industrial engineering, statistics, or physics (per earlier-confirmed official UOC page text already in the candidates file; not independently re-extracted in full this session due to 301 redirect/404 issues on direct refetch).
admission_requirements.credential_recognition_note: Not found — non-EU credential legalization process not located on reachable pages.
admission_requirements.other: URV is the degree-granting/coordinating university; UOC delivers the online teaching (joint interuniversity program).

language_requirements.english_certificate_required: No formal certificate requirement found. A 2021/22 student guide (EIMT-UOC, via SlideShare) states 'the vehicular language for teaching the master is English' and that students must be able to read scientific-technical texts in English since some materials exist only in English — but this is informal guidance, not a stated IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge threshold.

Subject area: computational engineering and applied/computational mathematics (modelling, numerical methods, computational methods) rather than an EE/hardware program.
